requirements.text: Two consent grants made at the same time from different worktrees of one clone are both kept
A vbw command interrupted mid-commit leaves no stray index files in .vbw/runtime and keeps the caller's own exit cleanup
vbw report and vbw rtk do what their help says
In a real session, a documentation requirement is built by the Docs agent and proved
In a real session, QA fails a phase whose build deviates from its plan, and the fix loop closes it
In balanced autonomy, a background QA run causes no Stop-hook errors and the session reaches the accept stop
Blocking or resetting a plan (its note or status) never withdraws the user's approval of an unchanged contract
Accepting a [human] requirement closes only the fixes opened by the user's own rejections; a fix QA opened stays open until QA passes the phase again
QA cannot record a verdict on a proof older than the current code: vbw qa record refuses and asks for vbw prove first
While one session's VBW run is open, vbw next in another session says the run belongs to another session and to wait or check status; it never tells that session to end the run
vbw run end from a session that does not own the open run is refused, unless the user states that the owning session is closed or the run is older than 24 hours
While a run is open, another session, neither its main conversation nor its agents, can edit the files that run is writing
Turning on autonomous mode in one session leaves it on in every other session where it was on

tools/baseline holds the plan's seven benchmark cases (fix-oneshot, failing-check fix, brownfield feature, safety-destructive, safety-secret, hostile-repo, markdown deliverable), each with a deterministic pass/fail check that fails on the untouched starting project and passes on a correct solution
The benchmark has run every case 3 times with plain Claude Code and 3 times with VBW 2, on Sonnet 5.5 and on Opus 5.5, and its committed results record each run's pass or fail, tokens and cost
docs/benchmark.md compares VBW 2 with plain Claude Code case by case, shows VBW 1 from its recorded runs and behaviour ledger, and states plainly what was not measured
README.md presents VBW 2 to someone new: what it does and why, how to install it, a first project, the commands, with images
CONTRIBUTING.md and the repository's other contributor files describe VBW 2 only: every command, path and tool they name exists

phases.title: Kernel safety: concurrent consent and interrupted commits
phases.goal: The kernel never loses a consent grant and never leaves debris when a command is interrupted.
criteria: A test starts two consent grants at once from two worktrees of one clone, and both grants are in consent.json afterwards.
That test fails on the pre-fix code, and the failure is shown.
A test interrupts a vbw commit mid-way, and .vbw/runtime holds no stray index files afterwards.
A test sets a caller EXIT trap, interrupts the commit, and the caller's trap still runs.
Both tests pass under /bin/bash 3.2 and bash 5, and bash tools/test.sh passes in full.
The kernel is still within 3,000 lines.

phases.title: Honest report and rtk commands
phases.goal: vbw report and vbw rtk behave as their --help text says.
criteria: Each claim in the help text of vbw report and vbw rtk has a test that runs the command and checks the stated outcome.
Where the command and its help disagreed, one was corrected, and a regression test fails without that correction.
The help text and the user docs (docs/) say the same thing about both commands.
bash tools/test.sh passes in full.

phases.title: Balanced autonomy: background QA reaches the accept stop
phases.goal: In balanced autonomy, a background QA run ends cleanly and the session reaches the accept stop.
criteria: An L3 scenario in tools/l3-suite.sh runs balanced autonomy with a background QA run on a named fixture.
The session transcript and debug log hold zero Stop-hook errors during that run.
The record shows the session stopped at the accept stop.
The L3 result names its fixture, its cost and its evidence level.

phases.title: Docs agent builds a documentation requirement
phases.goal: A documentation requirement is built by the Docs agent and proved in a real session.
criteria: An L3 scenario drives /vbw:vibe on a fixture whose spec has one documentation requirement.
The record shows the Docs agent built it, by agent type.
The requirement's check is approved and passes in the record, and the commit carries provenance.
The result is logged with fixture, cost and evidence level.

phases.title: QA fails a deviating build and the fix loop closes it
phases.goal: QA fails a phase whose build deviates from its plan, and the fix loop brings it back to passing.
criteria: An L3 scenario seeds a build that deviates from its plan (a named deviation, e.g. a file the plan requires is missing).
The record shows the QA verdict as fail and names that deviation.
The record shows at least one fix iteration, then a QA verdict of pass.
The phase ends proved, and the number of fix rounds is logged.

phases.title: Approval survives blocking and resetting a plan
phases.goal: Blocking or resetting a plan never withdraws the user's approval of a contract whose content is unchanged.
criteria: With an approved contract, setting a plan's note leaves the contract approval in place and the approved hash unchanged
With an approved contract, blocking a plan leaves the approval in place
With an approved contract, resetting a plan's status leaves the approval in place
Changing the contract content (a requirement, check or plan definition) still withdraws the approval
After block or reset on an unchanged contract, the next vbw next --json proceeds without asking for re-approval
Each case has a bats regression test that fails without the fix, and bash tools/test.sh passes under /bin/bash 3.2 and bash 5
The kernel stays within its 3,000-line budget

phases.title: Accept closes only the user's own fixes
phases.goal: Accepting a [human] requirement closes only the fixes opened by the user's own rejections, and leaves QA-opened fixes open until QA passes the phase again.
criteria: Test: a user rejection opens a fix, and a later accept of that requirement closes it.
Test: a fix opened by QA stays open after the user accepts the requirement.
Test: the QA-opened fix closes only when QA records a passing verdict for the phase.
Each regression test fails when run against the code before the fix.
R11 shows as proven in `vbw show requirements`, and bash tools/test.sh passes.

phases.title: QA verdicts require a fresh proof
phases.goal: vbw qa record refuses to record a verdict on a proof older than the current code and tells the caller to run vbw prove first.
criteria: Test: after a code change since the last vbw prove, `vbw qa record` exits non-zero and writes nothing to the record.
The refusal message names `vbw prove` as the next step.
Test: after vbw prove, the same `vbw qa record` succeeds.
The QA agent and workflow handle the refusal by running prove and retrying, and a test covers that path.
The kernel stays within its 3,000-line budget, checked by tests/standards.bats.
R12 shows as proven in `vbw show requirements`.

phases.title: Run ownership across sessions
phases.goal: A session that does not own the open run is told to wait or check status, and cannot end that run except by the stated exceptions.
criteria: With a run open in session A, `vbw next` in session B reports that the run belongs to another session and advises waiting or `vbw status`; its output contains no instruction to end the run.
`vbw run end` from session B is refused with a non-zero exit and the run stays open in the record.
`vbw run end` from session B succeeds when the user states that the owning session is closed.
`vbw run end` from session B succeeds when the open run is older than 24 hours (tested with a run whose start time is 25 hours old) and is refused at 23 hours.
`vbw run end` from the owning session still succeeds.
Bats tests cover each case above, each shown to fail before the change, and `bash tools/test.sh` passes under bash 3.2 and bash 5.

phases.title: Guard the files an open run is writing
phases.goal: While a run is open, no other session, neither its main conversation nor its agents, can edit the files that run is writing, unless the user states the owner is closed (D11).
criteria: With a run open in session A that writes file F, an Edit or Write of F from session B's main conversation is blocked by the hook with a message naming the owning session.
The same edit from a subagent of session B is blocked.
Files the run is not writing remain editable from session B.
Session A and its own agents can still edit F.
After the user states the owning session is closed, the edit from session B is allowed.
Outside a VBW project or with no open run, the hook allows edits and stays within the 8 ms hook CPU budget (`tools/bench-hooks.sh`).
Bats tests cover each case, shown to fail before the change.

phases.title: Autonomous mode per session
phases.goal: Turning on autonomous mode in one session never turns it off in any other session where it was on.
criteria: Turn autonomy on in session A, then on in session B: session A still reports autonomy on.
Turn it on in B first and then A: both still report on, in either order.
Concurrent turn-on calls from two sessions both persist (no lost update), checked by a parallel test.
Turning it off in one session is the only way that session changes, and other sessions are unaffected.
Bats tests cover each case, shown to fail before the change, and the full suite passes under bash 3.2 and bash 5.

phases.title: Contributor files describe VBW 2 only
phases.goal: CONTRIBUTING.md and the other contributor files (AGENTS.md, .github templates, copilot-instructions, CODEOWNERS, workflows docs) name only commands, paths and tools that exist in VBW 2.
criteria: A test script extracts every command, path and tool named in CONTRIBUTING.md, AGENTS.md, .github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE.md, .github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/* and .github/copilot-instructions.md and exits 0 only if each exists in the repository
No contributor file mentions .vbw-planning, v1 slash commands or v1 scripts that are absent from the tree (grep returns no match)
The check is part of bash tools/test.sh and fails on a file that names a nonexistent path (shown by a selftest)
bash tools/test.sh passes under /bin/bash 3.2 and bash 5

phases.title: Benchmark cases with deterministic checks
phases.goal: tools/baseline holds the seven benchmark cases, each with a deterministic pass/fail check that fails on the untouched start and passes on a correct solution.
criteria: tools/baseline/cases has exactly seven cases: fix-oneshot, failing-check fix, brownfield feature, safety-destructive, safety-secret, hostile-repo, markdown deliverable
For each case, running its check on the untouched fixture exits non-zero
For each case, running its check on a committed known-correct solution exits zero
A bats test runs all seven pairs of checks and fails if any case lacks either result
tools/baseline/README.md names each case, its fixture and its check

phases.title: Benchmark run harness and full run (84 runs)
phases.goal: Every case has run 3 times with plain Claude Code and 3 times with VBW 2, on Sonnet 5.5 and Opus 5.5, with each run's pass or fail, tokens and cost committed.
criteria: tools/baseline/results holds a committed record for each of the 84 runs (7 cases x 2 arms x 2 models x 3), each with arm, model, case, pass or fail, tokens and cost
A script verifies the results set is complete (84 distinct runs, no missing field) and the check is in bash tools/test.sh
Runs paused by a usage limit are resumed, none dropped or silently replaced; any re-run is recorded as such
Results are marked at L2 evidence level (scripted headless runs) with the fixtures named
Depends on P2 (the cases must be validated before any run)

criteria: docs/benchmark.md has one section per case with VBW 2 and plain Claude Code pass rate, tokens and cost for both models, with every number traceable to a committed result file
VBW 1 is shown from its recorded fix-oneshot baseline runs and the behaviour ledger, labelled inferred, with no new VBW 1 runs
A Not measured section names the gaps (VBW 1 cases without data, evidence level L2, sample size of 3)
The owner reads the document and accepts or rejects it (human requirement)
Depends on P3

todos.text: Screenshot kept with a visual accept verdict (was R9 of M1; the user attaches it per D1)
vbw prove runs the approved checks in parallel (today one after another), so every user's proof is faster
QA round runs the project's full test suite once and hands the result to the QA agents, not one run per agent (load spikes made the hook benchmark fail: F2, F5)

Two sessions on one project: the run lease does not record its session, so a second session is told to end the first session's live run as 'interrupted'. Record the owning session in the lease; other sessions wait unless it is stale.

Status line says what is happening now: set refreshInterval so it stays current while the session waits on background work; one clear state (VBW working: what, for how long / waiting for you: what / idle); and a 'vbw activity' note for long work outside a VBW run (releases, test runs), shown until done

Enforce the unenforced budgets: a status line CPU benchmark (30 ms), and prompt budget tests by one documented token estimate (router 2k, each skill 3k, all prompts 15k); trim if they show it (owner: not critical before the merge)

decisions.text: F3: keep tests/kernel-safety.bats test 2 as a regression test; it is not expected to fail on pre-fix code

Removing a true test would only reduce coverage.
